newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end sharply lower with soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end sharply lower with soybeans.

text.p: A strong weather-related sell-off in CBOT soybean futures caused soymeal and soyoil to end the session with heavy losses on Monday, CBOT floor traders said.
"Weather is ruling the soy complex right now, and the weather is good for the crops and bearish for futures," said one commission house trader.
Near the market open, all nearby soyoil months scored fresh contract lows, and July soymeal futures plunged to the lowest level in nearly three months.
Data from Friday's Commitments of Traders report from the CFTC was also seen as very bearish for soymeal futures, traders said.
"With the commitments, the meal was the really scary one," said one commission house trader.
The report revealed that commodity funds had been adding to their long positions last week just as the market peaked, so heavy liquidation is inevitable, the trader said.
July soyoil futures settled down 0.23 cent per lb at 23.23, with other months 0.17 to 0.27 cent lower. July soymeal closed down $8.80 per ton at $264.80 and other months were $2.00 to $8.00 lower.
